text:
sophie: Heads up — after the canary of gpu-operator 1.9.0 to a small subset of eu-west nodes we started seeing a cluster of GPU pods stuck in Pending and a few jobs reporting NCCL init failures. Can confirm this is ~5 nodes so far.

raj: Looking now. kubelet logs show the driver-manager daemonset repeatedly crashlooping on affected nodes. Error snippet from node-12: ```Apr 20 03:14:22 kubelet[2345]: driver-manager: failed to load module nvidia_modeset: operation not permitted
Apr 20 03:14:22 driver-manager: exiting with code 1```

maria: gpu-operator canary was configured to enable the new "auto-driver-update" feature in 1.9.0. Those nodes are on kernel 6.1.x. Could be module mismatch.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout complete to 5 nodes (eu-west-1a) @1729001200.

tim: we saw a similar pattern last year when dkms couldn't build against newer kernel headers — deviceplugin advertised 0 GPUs until module probe completed. Are /dev/nvidia* present on the host?

raj: On node-12 there are no nvidia devices. dmesg shows: "nvidia: probe of nvidia failed with -2". Also device-plugin logs show: "DevicePlugin: health check failed, reported 0 devices"

sophie: Some workloads fell back to us-west due to smart routing; autoscaler spun up extra instances which increased cost for the day (~$3.2k). Noted for billing. :grimacing:

maria: Immediate mitigation: recommend pinning gpu-operator image back to 1.8.4 and disabling auto-driver-update. That should stop the daemonset restarts and let nodes reprobe.

oncall-ops: Taking action now — cordoning affected nodes, initiating rollback of gpu-operator to 1.8.4 in eu-west, and adding node annotation to force device-plugin re-probe. I'll post updates. :hammer_and_wrench:

tim: Drain is failing on a few jobs that use local storage. We'll do a partial drain + taint so scheduling avoids them until driver state stabilizes.

raj: Quick config note — if the operator tries to replace driver with image that expects kernel module build toolchain, dkms must be installed and host kernel headers available. Canary nodes were missing headers due to faster AMI churn in eu-west.

sophie: Also seeing some NCCL errors on ML jobs that did get scheduled: "NCCL WARN Call to cuInit failed: 999" then timeout. Likely because clients couldn't see GPUs during init window.

maria: Agreed. After rollback we should run a kubelet preflight that verifies: /dev/nvidia* present, nvidia-smi returns 0 GPUs? and device-plugin reports non-empty list before rolling further canaries. Add that to canary gating.

oncall-ops: Rollback started @1729002500. gpu-operator 1.8.4 applied and auto-driver-update disabled. Re-probing nodes; device-plugin now shows devices on node-12.

raj: Confirmed: device-plugin reports 8 GPUs on node-12 now, driver-manager stable. No more crashloops in last 7m.

tim: I'll open an infra ticket to add AMI validation to our image build pipeline to ensure kernel-headers + dkms are present for GPU AMIs. Also adding a canary gating check to CI.

sophie: Filing postmortem and tagging cost impact. We should also add a runbook step: if device-plugin reports 0 devices after operator rollout, check kernel headers and DKMS before draining.

maria: Agree. We'll schedule a delayed staged rollout for 1.9.0 once we have preflight checks and AMI fixes.

infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-142, severity: low, owner: oncall-ops.

sophie: Thanks team. Keep threads here for updates. :eyes:
